Imperative vs declarative
How imperative code differs from declarative in JavaScript: swapping a loop with push for filter and a predicate, then raising the abstraction with filterBy.
Understand the difference between imperative code, which tells you how you do it, and declarative code, which tells you what the code does, and learn to rewrite a loop with filter and a predicate.
text
Imperative code tells you "how you do it". In other words, you have to dig into the code itself.

Declarative code tells you what your code does; it is more often modular, and you do not need to dig into the whole codebase. If changes are needed, you make them in a specific section of the code in a modular way.

filter with the isGt3 predicate replaces a loop with a condition and push: we don't dig into the implementation, we just read the name.
The level of abstraction can be raised further: gt(2) creates a predicate, and filterBy(gt2) creates a filtering function that waits for an array. The name filterByGt2 already tells you what it does.
